title: SoftBank Is Said to Weigh Buying Top US Security Firm Allied
source_used: Investing.com text on Yahoo Finance (relay of Bloomberg); Bloomberg itself is behind a robot check
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on Friday 16 Oct 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that SoftBank Group is weighing the purchase of Allied Universal, the largest US security services company.
Equity value could reach $18 billion; including about $12 billion of publicly traded debt the deal could come to close to $30 billion.
Talks are preliminary; no final decisions on a deal or price.
Allied Universal supplies security personnel for businesses, events and infrastructure, including New York City's subway through contracts with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
It also offers intelligence analysis, canine units, bomb technicians, cleaning, janitorial and facility maintenance, and has a significant presence in security for data center building.
Founder Masayoshi Son sees the labor-heavy security business as a possible testing ground for robots built by SoftBank's portfolio companies.
quote_evidence: Discussions remain preliminary, and no final decisions have been made on a deal or its price.
Allied Universal provides security personnel for businesses, events and infrastructure, including New York City's subway system through contracts with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
why_it_matters_hint: A possible SoftBank purchase of the largest US security firm, with robots as the stated aim, but nothing is decided.
notes: Same story as C11-04 (this one is the Bloomberg original, Reuters citing Bloomberg also carried it). Bloomberg page blocked; facts from the Investing.com copy on Yahoo Finance. Reuters headline says $18 billion (equity only).
